questions.question: Which site-note sentence is clearest and most professional?
answers: Opening wrong. What do you want me to do?
The opening is not right but we can probably make it work.
Need an answer ASAP because this is holding us up.
The opening is 15 mm narrower than the drawing; please confirm the required dimension before work continues.
questions.explanation: A professional note states the issue, gives the relevant fact and asks for a clear decision.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a colon correctly?
answers: Bring the following: PPE safety boots, gloves and eye protection.
Bring the following PPE safety boots: gloves and eye protection.
Bring the following PPE: safety boots, gloves and eye protection.
Bring: the following PPE safety boots, gloves and eye protection.
questions.explanation: A colon can introduce a list after a complete lead-in.

questions.question: A supervisor writes, “Do not proceed until the revised detail has been issued.” What does this require?
answers: Ask a colleague which detail they would use.
Stop the relevant work and wait for the revised detail.
Continue but leave the final section unfinished.
Use the previous detail unless told otherwise.
questions.explanation: The instruction explicitly prevents the work from proceeding until revised information is issued.

questions.question: Which sentence gives the least ambiguous instruction?
answers: Measure from the marked datum to the left-hand edge of the opening.
Measure it from there to the opening.
Take the measurement to the side.
Measure from the mark to the edge.
questions.explanation: It names both the starting point and the exact finishing point.

questions.question: Which sentence is written in the active voice?
answers: The dimensions were checked before cutting.
The dimensions had been checked by the apprentice.
Before cutting, the dimensions were being checked.
The apprentice checked the dimensions before cutting.
questions.explanation: The subject performs the action directly in the active voice.

questions.question: Which sentence is most appropriate for a formal work record?
answers: The thing was bad so we stopped.
Component looked rough; told someone.
The damaged component was isolated and reported to the supervisor at 10:20.
I sorted the dodgy bit and told the boss.
questions.explanation: A formal record is specific, factual and time-linked.

questions.question: Which sentence reports an observation rather than an assumption?
answers: The wall was built incorrectly.
Water is visible at the base of the wall after rainfall.
The DPC has definitely failed.
Someone must have damaged the membrane.
questions.explanation: An observation states what can actually be seen without guessing the cause.

questions.question: Which question is most useful when a drawing note is unclear?
answers: Which revision and detail should I follow for this opening?
Is this right?
What am I supposed to do?
Can somebody sort this?
questions.explanation: It identifies the precise information needed to resolve the ambiguity.

questions.question: A report says, “The temporary repair reduced the leak but did not eliminate it.” Which conclusion is supported?
answers: The permanent repair has been completed.
The leak was caused by the temporary repair.
No further monitoring is necessary.
The problem still requires further action.
questions.explanation: The statement says the leak remains, so further action is still needed.

questions.question: Which sequence makes an incident note easiest to understand?
answers: Who was informed → unrelated history → action → guess
Opinion → cause → action → what happened
What happened → immediate action → who was informed → next action
Next action → opinion → what happened → blame
questions.explanation: A chronological factual sequence makes the record clear and auditable.

questions.question: A note says “verify dimensions on site before manufacture.” What does “verify” mean here?
answers: copy the dimensions without checking
check and confirm that the dimensions are correct
estimate the dimensions from the drawing
change the dimensions to suit available stock
questions.explanation: To verify is to check and confirm accuracy.

questions.question: Which message best explains a delay to a customer?
answers: The repair is delayed because the replacement part has not arrived. We will confirm a new completion time when delivery is verified.
We are running late because the part is not here.
It will not be done today. Sorry.
Supplier problem, nothing we can do.
questions.explanation: It gives the reason, impact and next communication clearly and professionally.

questions.question: Which statement is a fact rather than an opinion?
answers: The opening looks badly built.
The installer did a poor job.
The opening is probably too small because someone rushed.
The measured opening is 905 mm wide.
questions.explanation: A measured dimension can be checked objectively.

questions.question: Which instruction is ordered most logically?
answers: Prove isolation, begin the work, then isolate the supply.
Begin the permitted work and isolate the supply if needed.
Isolate the supply, prove it is isolated, then begin the permitted work.
Begin the work, isolate the supply, then prove isolation.
questions.explanation: The sequence places isolation and confirmation before work begins.

questions.question: Which sentence avoids unnecessary blame in a defect report?
answers: The supplier keeps sending us rubbish.
The unit was found damaged on inspection and has been quarantined pending review.
The delivery driver obviously broke the unit.
Someone has damaged this again.
questions.explanation: A professional defect report records facts and action without unsupported blame.

questions.question: What does “retain for inspection” mean?
answers: keep the item available so it can be examined
dispose of the item after photographing it
return the item immediately
continue using the item until someone arrives
questions.explanation: To retain something is to keep it rather than discard or return it.

questions.question: A drawing note says “typ.” beside several identical details. What is the safest reading approach?
answers: Assume every detail in the project is identical.
Ignore the note because only dimensions matter.
Use the note only at the first location shown.
Treat it as applying to similar locations, but check any location that differs or conflicts.
questions.explanation: A typical detail can apply repeatedly, but differences and conflicts still need checking.

questions.question: Which sentence is most suitable for a handover note?
answers: Finished everything and tidied up.
Job sorted, customer happy.
Work completed to the issued detail; final fixings checked; area left clean and access restored.
Done. Looks fine.
questions.explanation: A handover note should state what was completed and the relevant checks or condition.

questions.question: Which phrase most clearly signals a mandatory requirement?
answers: may be installed
must be installed
should preferably be installed
could be installed
questions.explanation: “Must” indicates a requirement rather than a recommendation or option.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly distinguishes advice from instruction?
answers: The guidance recommends a method, but the specification requires the stated finish.
The guidance and specification are always optional.
A recommendation automatically overrides the specification.
The specification is only advice if guidance exists.
questions.explanation: Recommendations and mandatory project requirements do not have the same status.

questions.question: A report states “no defect was visible at the time of inspection.” What does this NOT prove?
answers: that the inspector did not see a defect at that time
that the inspection occurred
that the report records the observation
that no hidden or intermittent defect exists
questions.explanation: The wording is limited to what was visible at that time.

questions.question: Which sentence gives the clearest comparison?
answers: It is 8 mm different.
The measurements are not the same by 8 mm.
The second measurement is 8 mm greater than the first.
The second one is bigger.
questions.explanation: It identifies which value is greater and by exactly how much.

questions.question: A customer says, “It only leaks when the wind drives rain from the west.” Which detail is most important to record?
answers: the colour of the internal decoration
the weather condition and direction associated with the leak
the customer’s opinion of the previous repair
the time the operative normally starts work
questions.explanation: The condition under which the fault appears is useful diagnostic information.

questions.question: Which sentence is the strongest summary of a completed check?
answers: Level, line and fixing positions were checked against the issued drawing before handover.
I checked it all and it was okay.
Everything seemed right before I left.
The work was checked as usual.
questions.explanation: It names the checks and the reference used.

questions.question: Which response best checks understanding after receiving a complex verbal instruction?
answers: Okay, I think I have got it.
I will work it out as I go.
Can you just leave me to it?
So I will isolate the area, check the revised dimensions, then call you before fixing — is that correct?
questions.explanation: Restating the key sequence gives the other person a chance to correct misunderstanding.
